scope.summary: Implement the proximity/contact driver (spec 13.19; PREQ-018/019 foundation): a typed ProximityDriver sampling surface distance and signed penetration depth from a designated penetrator or contact collider to a receiver region (including canal-parameterized orifice axes), emitting a normalized 0..1 value that drives corrective weights - the foundation MT-556 orifice penetration correctives build on.
acceptance_criteria: ProximityDriver samples surface distance plus signed penetration depth along a canal axis where a receiver defines one, and outputs a normalized 0..1 driver value streamed to corrective weights per frame.
Driver graph edges are explicit, named, and inspectable per the MT-496 anti-ERC discipline; per-edge disable works and no hidden links exist.
Canal-parameterized receiver API contract lands here (registration, axis definition, depth normalization) even though vaginal/anal/oral receivers register later in BkGenitals (MT-549/553/556).
Determinism: identical scene states produce identical driver values, and values are recorded in TraceProjection for debugging.
scope.risk_if_missed: MT-556 orifice correctives and all penetration-driven deformation depend on this signal; without a deterministic proximity/depth driver, penetration scenes need hand-keyed morphs per frame and the driver graph accretes hidden ad-hoc couplings that violate the decouple law.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit morphs and correctives

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT emits typed diagnostics through its owning command or job and inherits retention, health, and projection behavior from the shared diagnostics substrate.
The owning native shell or scheduled job supplies Palmistry coverage; this MT must preserve operation identity and recovery handles.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.
